about: Guided tracks (docs/library/TRACKS.md). One source for the tracks and the reading paths. A track is live only when every step has a page and a check with status: reviewed. pathName shows the step in the 'Next on your path' box. A track with a "home" field is listed on that path's card on the library home page (the card's heading id).

tracks.name: New parent judge
tracks.title: New Parent Judge Track: Judge Your First Debate Round
tracks.description: A free, self-paced track for new policy debate judges. Six short pages, each with a quick check. About 50 minutes. Progress stays in your browser.
tracks.promise: You can judge a fair round today.

tracks.name: Novice debater
tracks.title: Novice Debater Track: Learn the Core Arguments
tracks.description: A free, self-paced track for first-year policy debaters: speeches, flowing, the aff case, DAs, counterplans, topicality and weighing, with checks.
tracks.promise: You can run and answer the core arguments.

tracks.name: Intro to the K
tracks.title: Intro to the Kritik: A Guided Policy Debate Track
tracks.description: A free, self-paced track on kritiks: the link, the alternative, the role of the ballot, framework and how to answer a K, with a quick check after each page.
tracks.promise: You can explain and answer a basic kritik.

tracks.name: Theory basics
tracks.title: Debate Theory Basics: A Guided Policy Debate Track
tracks.description: A free, self-paced track on theory: the parts of a theory argument, fiat, conditionality and reasons to reject, with a quick check after each page.
tracks.promise: You can read, run and answer a basic theory argument.

tracks.name: Judging well
tracks.title: Judging Well: A Guided Track for Experienced Debate Judges
tracks.description: A free, self-paced track for judges past their first rounds: paradigms, the RFD, presumption, turns case, round conduct, feedback and writing a paradigm.
tracks.promise: You can decide close rounds and explain them well.
